title: (Obj) for the constructible cocone
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $X$ a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian. The
constructible cocone ([def-sfb-constructible-cocone]) satisfies (Obj) of
[sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit]: every $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to
$T_{E,\Qlb}K_E$ for some finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$ and some
$K_E\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-constructible-cocone-ambient-realization] to identify the coefficient and constructibility conventions and to realize the specified cocone by triangulated functors $\Phi_E:\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal D=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Omega_X})$, with its given transition comparisons.

source.place: Complexes paragraph: scalar extension, inherited triangles, and the connecting morphism; Modules paragraph: the coefficient and local-presentation conventions

proof.text: Put $P(Y)\iff\exists E,\exists K_E\in\mathcal C_E,\ Y\cong\Phi_E(K_E)$. The field index is nonempty. Since the vertex is full in $\mathcal D$, Hom-surjectivity lifts every ambient arrow between two images to a common finite stage, with precisely the comparisons from step 1. Apply the directed-triangulated-image lemma: $P$ is triangulated. Composing its witnessing isomorphisms makes $P$ isomorphism-closed.

source.place: Complexes paragraph: scalar extension, inherited triangles, and the connecting morphism; Modules paragraph: the coefficient and local-presentation conventions

proof.text: For a constructible $\Omega_X$-module $M$, finite-presentation descent gives a constructible $E_X$-module $M_E$ and $\Omega_X\otimes_{E_X}M_E\cong M$, using the identification in step 1. The single complex $M_E[0]$ is bounded constructible: only $H^0=M_E$ is nonzero, and zero has presentation $0\to0\to0$. By the termwise exact scalar-extension realization in step 1 and exact-derived-functor compatibility with single complexes, $\Phi_E(M_E[0])\cong M[0]$. Thus $P(M[0])$.

source.place: Complexes paragraph: scalar extension, inherited triangles, and the connecting morphism; Modules paragraph: the coefficient and local-presentation conventions

proof.text: Apply finite truncation devissage to $\Omega_X$ and $P$. Step 2 supplies a triangulated, isomorphism-closed property; step 3 supplies all constructible degree-zero objects. Therefore $P(K)$ for every bounded constructible $K$.

source.place: Complexes paragraph: scalar extension, inherited triangles, and the connecting morphism; Modules paragraph: the coefficient and local-presentation conventions

proof.text: Unpack $P(K)$. Both $K$ and $\Phi_E(K_E)$ belong to the full cocone vertex, so the ambient isomorphism and its inverse are vertex morphisms. They give exactly (Obj) for the specified cocone.
